title: II. Eternal life defined; why called life and eternal
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): 3:3). We call it eternal to differ both out from temporal bodily life plus out from ye faithful's spiritual life in this world, ye which stands as a degree plus beginning belonging toward such that eternal life now hidden together with Christ in God (Col. We call it life by metonymy belonging toward ye subject unto ye elect's beatitude in a protected plus youthful state — here to live stands as to be blessed. || Eternal life stands as ye citizens belonging toward God's kingdom's absolute immunity out from sin, Satan plus ye tyranny belonging toward ye impious, plus every misery, plus joined together with this ye eternal plus fullest fruition belonging toward every good in ye blessed vision plus communion belonging toward God, perfect glorification belonging toward soul plus body, restoration belonging toward ye divine image, most joyful fellowship belonging toward holy angels plus all ye pious, plus unexhausted joy unto perfectly celebrating God's glory. II.
pass_b_english: II. Eternal life is the citizens of God's kingdom's absolute immunity from sin, Satan and the tyranny of the impious, and every misery, and joined with this the eternal and fullest fruition of every good in the blessed vision and communion of God, perfect glorification of soul and body, restoration of the divine image, most joyful fellowship of holy angels and all the pious, and unexhausted joy for perfectly celebrating God's glory.

We call it life by metonymy of the subject for the elect's beatitude in a protected and youthful state — here to live is to be blessed. We call it eternal to differ both from temporal bodily life and from the faithful's spiritual life in this world, which is a degree and beginning of that eternal life now hidden with Christ in God (Col. 3:3).
source_text: II. Vita aeterna est civium regni Dei absoluta immunitas a peccato, Satana & impiorum tyrannide, omnique miseria, & cum hac conjuncta aeterna & plenissima omnis boni fruitio in beata Dei visione & communione, perfecta animae & corporis glorificatione, divinae imaginis instauratione, consortio sanctorum angelorum omniumque piorum jucundissimo, laetitia inexhausta ad Dei gloriam perfecte celebrandam. Vitam dicimus electorum beatitudinem protecto & juventium statu, per metonymiam subjecti — hic vivere est beatum esse. Aeternam dicimus ad differentiam tum vitae corporalis temporalis, tum spiritualis fidelium in hoc mundo, quae est gradus & principium aeternae illius vitae nunc absconditae cum Christo in Deo, Col. 3.v.3.
